claim_one_line: THE V1 CARD, RUN ON MAIN AND READ ONCE (the audit's finding that the nulls behind the six's rarities have an unpriced window in the height of the modulus; the advisor seat's sealed card, the deciding count run by main on random targets only, its two output files committed unread at 818d17f46 before either was opened; a million targets a null, 8,625 seconds): ALL THREE DECISIVE CELLS READ B, an end of the window is like other rows, so by the card's rule, fixed before any number, the finding is reduced to one sentence for these two nulls -- B1726's null under the worst factor loses 109 of its best thousand targets when the top layer is removed (1.64 times that layer's share of the rows; 24 targets short of the card's line at twice the share), B1753's loses 134 under chi-squared (1.99; short by less than one target) and 132 under the worst factor (1.96; short by three), and every bottom end reads C (4, 6 and 6 lost: the reach of the well-fitted targets ends inside the window there). Main recomputed every reading from its counts with its own exact interval. At ten times the sample, the best 1 per cent, the three ratios are 1.46, 1.90 and 1.89. UNDER THE COVARIANT AND FREE MENUS, WHICH THE CARD MAKES READ-OUTS, THE SECOND NULL'S TOP END READS A BY THE SAME RULE at both depths (2.0 to 2.4), and the first null's reads B under every menu. THE AUDIT'S FIGURE IS REPRODUCED AND IS NOT ABOUT RARITY: 20.6 per cent of all random targets of the first null have their least bad row in the top layer, three times its share and far above its neighbours, while among the well-fitted the last layer is below its neighbour in every decisive cell -- the pile-up at the edge belongs to targets that fit nothing. Recorded: the sentence, with the measured factor (a higher top end would add well-fitted random targets about 1.5 times as fast as rows for the first null and about 2 times for the second; a lower bottom end almost none), as dated notes in the two arcs that own the rarities and on the law map's row; owed (P-786): the same sentence on the other pages that quote either rarity, the window's two ends listed as a choice in the input budget, the same count on the live candidate's null before its card is sealed, and the seat's own verdict. Main's expectations before the run leaned further towards A than the seat's; the decisive cells went the seat's way, narrowly, and a count can differ by a few targets on another machine. No rarity is re-read, no measured target enters, and nothing is compared with a measurement. 0 of 19.
